_doc: Known-wrong statements the LLM must never assert (belge 03 s.11). Dates are the source file's own date; null = the source file carries none. All entries are the upstream project claims and must be re-verified against primary sources (Google Search Central, web.dev) before being stated as fact in a report.

facts.statement_wrong: FID (First Input Delay) is a Core Web Vitals metric.
facts.statement_right: INP replaced FID; FID was removed from CrUX and PageSpeed Insights on 2024-09-09.

facts.statement_wrong: 'Visual Stability Index' or 'Core Web Vitals 2.0' are real metrics.
facts.statement_right: LCP, INP and CLS are the entire CWV set.
HowTo rich results were deprecated (Sept 2023); never recommend HowTo schema.

facts.statement_wrong: Add FAQPage schema to get a Google SERP feature.
facts.statement_right: Per the source, Google retired FAQ rich results for all sites on 2026-05-07; do not recommend new FAQPage for a SERP benefit.

facts.statement_wrong: GPTBot status determines ChatGPT Search citation.
facts.statement_right: GPTBot is OpenAI's training crawler; ChatGPT Search uses OAI-SearchBot.

facts.statement_wrong: The Google-Extended robots rule controls AI Overviews inclusion.
facts.statement_right: AI Overviews follow Googlebot; Google-Extended governs Gemini/Vertex training and grounding.
Google Search ignores llms.txt; it is an optional signal for other systems.

facts.statement_wrong: Word count is a direct Google ranking factor.
facts.statement_right: Google does not use word count as a ranking factor; word thresholds are topical-coverage floors.

facts.statement_wrong: Google limits titles to 60 characters / descriptions to 160.
facts.statement_right: These are display heuristics, not a published search engine limit.

facts.statement_wrong: E-E-A-T is a Google ranking score with published weights.
facts.statement_right: E-E-A-T is a Quality Rater Guidelines concept; Google publishes no numeric weights.
